title: Build Your First Custom Image with a Dockerfile
description: Create a simple Dockerfile, build an image, and run a container from it.
problemStatement:
## Objective Write a Dockerfile that creates an image serving a static HTML page with Nginx. ### Steps 1. Create a new directory `my-web` and navigate into it. 2. Inside, create a subdirectory `html` and put an `index.html` file with some content (e.g., `

Hello from Docker!

`). 3. Create a file named `Dockerfile` with the following content: ```dockerfile FROM nginx:alpine COPY ./html /usr/share/nginx/html ``` 4. Build the image and tag it `my-web:1.0`: ```bash docker build -t my-web:1.0 . ``` 5. Run a container from the image, mapping port 8080 to 80: ```bash docker run -d --name web1 -p 8080:80 my-web:1.0 ``` 6. Open `http://localhost:8080` in your browser and verify your page is displayed. 7. Stop and remove the container. 8. (Optional) Improve the Dockerfile by adding a `LABEL` and an `EXPOSE` instruction. Rebuild and test. ### Deliverable Show the terminal output of `docker build` and a screenshot/curl of the served page.
hints: Ensure the `html` folder is in the build context (same directory as Dockerfile).
If port 8080 is already in use, choose another host port.
expectedOutput: A web page showing 'Hello from Docker!' when accessing localhost:8080.
solutionCode:
# Directory structure:
# my-web/
#   Dockerfile
#   html/
#     index.html

# Dockerfile content:
FROM nginx:alpine
COPY ./html /usr/share/nginx/html

# Build and run:
docker build -t my-web:1.0 .
docker run -d --name web1 -p 8080:80 my-web:1.0
curl http://localhost:8080
